markdown_report:
Select a conservative current-item readout gate after correcting padding execution. At 10% progress, this offers a small, family-preserving experiment before adding text or changing recurrent equations.

Starting-point insights: (1) A GRU state and current-item embedding offer complementary representations. Their usefulness together remains a hypothesis. (2) Sampled training errors range from 1.4% to 4.75%. Strong training separation does not establish validation HR@10. (3) Unpadded replay changes scores by up to 2.38. Consequently, existing deletion results cannot establish excessive historical influence.

Related-work insights: (1) PyTorch packing excludes padded recurrent steps when valid items are compacted first [1]. Packing left-padded inputs directly would truncate real interactions. (2) BPR-max emphasizes competitive negatives [2]. Its session-recommendation evidence does not establish Amazon gains. (3) Selective-memory recommendation motivates conditional weighting [3]. It does not validate another gate inside this GRU benchmark.

The framework separates three directions: execution correctness → trustworthy history interventions; ranking objectives → competitive-candidate separation; contextual readout → balancing current evidence and accumulated preferences. Execution correctness is a prerequisite for interpreting the other two.

Three atomic proposals follow. Scores are originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell includes a positive and negative assessment.

| Proposal | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regularized BPR-max [2] | 2: established; little novelty | 7: practical; transfer uncertain | 4: competitive ranking; no intent mechanism | 7: targets pair errors; training evidence only | 3: localized loss; sampling integration |
| **Current-item readout gate** [3] | 4: focused adaptation; familiar gating | 7: interpretable ablations; may overfit | 7: recent-specific evidence; ownership unobserved | 6: tests contextual separation; causal evidence absent | 3: two projections; export consistency required |
| Joint title encoder [4] | 5: attribute distinctions; established fusion | 7: specification sensitivity; sparse supervision | 8: relevance and compatibility cues; compatibility unverifiable | 5: harder distinctions; no text diagnostic | 6: one network; token pipeline needed |

The selected gate explicitly targets two user failures: broadly related items displacing specific matches, and insufficient weight on recent coherent interests. Its model-facing target is residual sampled ranking errors, especially Movies’ 4.75%; improvement remains unmeasured.

Compute ordinary GRU features hₜ and projected observed-item embedding uₜ. Set fₜ=(1−gₜ)hₜ+gₜuₜ, with gₜ=0.2·sigmoid(W[hₜ;uₜ]+b), initialized near 0.01. This limits the initial intervention while retaining historical context.

First establish padding and predictor consistency. Compare baseline loss against BPR-max separately; evaluate the gate with baseline loss to isolate architecture. Select solely through pinned macro validation HR@10, deploying one checkpoint per category. Neither gate values nor training margins demonstrate compatibility, unmet need, or validation gains.

References: [1] PyTorch packing/GRU documentation; [2] Hidasi and Karatzoglou, 2018; [3] Mamba4Rec, 2024; [4] MARS, 2024. Links appear in related work.

idea.description: Add a conservative coordinate-wise gate combining ordinary GRU4Rec features with the projected embedding of the currently observed item. Train all components jointly within one network per category. Establish padding-invariant execution first, then isolate this readout change from a separate regularized BPR-max objective experiment.
idea.motivation: The gate explicitly addresses two reported user-facing failures: broadly related recommendations displacing specific matches, and recent coherent interests receiving insufficient weight relative to broad historical interests. A direct current-item representation supplies recent evidence while the recurrent branch retains context. The measured model-facing target is residual sampled positive/negative ranking error: 4.75% in Movies_and_TV and 3.42% in Electronics. These measurements motivate testing but do not demonstrate harmful memory or predict validation improvement. Existing history-deletion results are confounded by padded recurrent updates. The gate cannot establish ownership needs, equipment compatibility, project intent, or desired quantities.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied corrected GRU4Rec rather than replacing its backbone. Inherit its dimensions, scoring function, dropout, optimizer, initialization and negative sampler unless explicitly testing the loss. The actual baseline source and numeric hyperparameters are absent from the prompt; do not invent a replacement training pipeline.

First verify padding semantics. If the supplied corrected baseline already skips padded recurrence, retain it. Otherwise compact real items in chronological order, pack only nonempty rows, run the existing GRU, and scatter outputs back to their original positions. Preserve empty-row behavior explicitly, with zero features and the baseline scoring bias if present. Apply the same implementation in ModelView and exported prediction. This correction requires retraining; do not interpret old checkpoints under changed recurrence. Verify evaluation scores for identical histories under extra leading padding, separate/batched execution, and training/export execution within declared numerical tolerances.

Let h_t be the baseline recommendation feature, with dimension D. Project the current observed item's learned embedding to D through P; use identity when dimensions match. Compute u_t=P(item_emb(sequence_t)), g_t=0.2*sigmoid(W_h*h_t+W_u*u_t+b), and f_t=(1-g_t)*h_t+g_t*u_t. Initialize W_h and W_u to zero and b=log(0.05/0.95), so g_t starts at 0.01. This is near-baseline, not exact identity. Preserve the baseline dropout locations and document where the new readout occurs. Zero padded features. Use f_t everywhere that the baseline uses recommendation features, retaining its candidate scorer. This is one jointly trained feature computation, without independent predictor fusion.

Predeclare a small experiment sequence: execution-correct ordinary baseline; baseline backbone with regularized BPR-max; gated readout with baseline loss. Evaluate a combined gate/BPR-max configuration only if the separate changes justify spending the remaining budget. All configurations are separate trials; never combine predictions. For an optional multi-negative objective comparison, use a shared prespecified candidate pool for its matched controls. Exclude padding, target IDs and known training positives, deduplicate candidates, and never consult validation/test positives to construct training exclusions. With negative scores s_j, define w=softmax(s_j), loss=-log(sum_j w_j*sigmoid(s_pos-s_j))+lambda*sum_j w_j*s_j^2. Implement the first term using log_softmax, logsigmoid and logsumexp for numerical stability. Record K and lambda before validation; their values are not specified by the supplied baseline. If the current baseline already uses equivalent BPR-max, omit the duplicate experiment.

Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), and the host ModelView contract, including supported candidate tensor shapes. Read the largest nonpadding position, never count-1. Save architecture settings and state_dict together. Update the embedded predictor writer with identical recurrence, projection, gate, readout and scoring definitions. Each of Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl loads exactly one selected checkpoint.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return measured metrics and definitions; view.model is the actual trained module. Keep the loader tuple and B x L tensors unchanged. Preserve valid-pair margins and error rates; add nonpadding gate quantiles and the relative norm of f_t-h_t. Record observation counts. Rerun the existing matched history interventions after padding checks pass, keeping populations, candidates and perturbation definitions fixed. Do not equate sensitivity with intent, near-zero mean embedding cosine with diversity, or anonymous rows with independent users. Missing category metadata and unmeasured export agreement must remain explicitly unavailable.

Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], artifacts beneath the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve supplied splits, all category routes, the pinned evaluator, and native recommendations for five training users per category. Use single-GPU execution and charge every trial, diagnostic and failure to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Select only through macro validation HR@10 over the four categories with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. No hidden tests, other-trial checkpoints, extra datasets, pretrained weights, unavailable metadata, independent fitted scores, or checkpoint averaging.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
set_preprocessing_seed(0)

# Integration specification: inherit the corrected host baseline implementation.
def log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    # Existing padding-safe baseline, or chronological compaction + packed GRU.
    h = ordinary_gru_features_aligned_to_original_positions(sequence)
    if variant == 'gated_readout':
        u = current_item_projection(item_emb(sequence))
        g = 0.2 * sigmoid(gate_h(h) + gate_u(u) + gate_bias)
        h = (1.0 - g) * h + g * u
    return where(valid[..., None], h, zeros_like(h))

def final_features(sequence, features):
    # Handle a zero-width sequence separately if the host supports it.
    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    index = where(sequence.ne(0), positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
    result = gather_time(features, index.clamp_min(0))
    return where(index[:, None].ge(0), result, zeros_like(result))

# Initially gate_h.weight=gate_u.weight=0; use one total bias log(0.05/0.95).
# Keep ordinary baseline scoring and diagnostic interfaces unchanged.
for prespecified_variant in affordable_experiment_sequence:
    for category in FOUR_REQUIRED_CATEGORIES:
        set_training_seed(42)
        model = construct_host_gru4rec(prespecified_variant)
        for epoch in range(at_most_200):
            for batch_index in range(200):
                _, sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                mask = host_valid_supervision_mask(sequence, positive, negative)
                if prespecified_variant == 'bpr_max':
                    candidates = training_only_unique_negative_pool()
                    s_pos, s_neg = model.score_training_candidates(features, positive, candidates)
                    log_w = log_softmax(s_neg, dim=-1)
                    ranking = -logsumexp(log_w + logsigmoid(s_pos[..., None]-s_neg), dim=-1)
                    regularizer = lambda_reg * (log_w.exp()*s_neg.square()).sum(dim=-1)
                    loss = masked_mean(ranking + regularizer, mask)
                else:
                    loss = host_baseline_loss(model, features, positive, negative, mask)
                host_optimizer_step(loss)
            apply_unchanged_host_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
        save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_architecture(category)
    write_matching_embedded_predictor_with_all_four_routes()
    verify_padding_and_export_score_agreement()
    retain_required_diagnostics_with_measured_definitions()
    submit_to_unchanged_host_macro_validation()

# Final prediction: load one selected model per category and use its single scorer.
# Never average checkpoints, networks, or separately fitted scores.

originality.positive: A bounded current-item gate offers a focused, falsifiable adaptation of the supplied GRU4Rec readout.
originality.negative: Gated feature combinations and recent-item skip connections are established; architectural novelty is incremental.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could reveal when direct recent evidence complements recurrent context and motivate later attribute-aware extensions.
future_potential.negative: The additional branch may overemphasize the latest purchase, and neither intent nor compatibility is observed.

code_difficulty.positive: The selected change adds small projections and a gate without replacing the GRU or adding a data pipeline.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding-safe recurrence, diagnostic alignment and exact predictor reconstruction require careful integration.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Defines packed sequence execution for variable-length recurrent inputs.
Supports excluding padded steps after chronological compaction of left-padded histories.
limitations: Directly packing left-padded tensors with valid lengths truncates real interactions.
Does not establish recommendation accuracy or runtime gains.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize competitive negatives.
Provides a direct GRU4Rec precedent for the separate objective experiment.
limitations: Session-recommendation findings do not establish gains under this Amazon protocol.
Negative sampling and regularization affect results and require controlled comparison.

related_work.title: Mamba4Rec: Towards Efficient Sequential Recommendation with Selective State Space Models
contributions: Studies selective state-space computation for sequential recommendation.
Motivates testing input-dependent weighting of sequential information.
limitations: Its backbone differs from GRU4Rec and cannot replace the required family.
Does not directly validate the proposed current-item readout gate.

related_work.title: MARS: Attribute-aware text representations for recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary describes attribute-aware representations that motivate finer item distinctions.
Inspires a deferred jointly trained title-encoder experiment.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model setting does not establish effectiveness with randomly initialized text features.
Textual similarity cannot establish equipment compatibility or unmet purchase needs.
